object_description: continuous low-rise perimeter frontage enclosing a green public garden
design_condition: The built frontage defines the block perimeter while varying its height toward residential and villa neighborhoods, enclosing a central public garden and connecting the school through a soft-mobility network.

positive.statement: The continuous frontage is successfully integrated through its low height and street-side gardens.

position.rationale: Perimeter mass and low stepped frontage are visible along the south-west garden edge.

positive.statement: The dimensions of the housing adapt judiciously to existing and future neighborhoods.

position.rationale: Approximate outer housing frontage is anchored on the east-south perimeter.

positive.statement: The school’s central position makes it visible from all sides and connects it to the different paths.

position.rationale: Central point-cloud mass is clearly surrounded by circulation and perimeter frontage.

positive.statement: The reception and transition space provides natural security for the exterior areas.

position.rationale: Likely entry transition is placed at the front ground-level edge; reception is not distinguishable.

positive.statement: The simple and functional program arrangement gives the younger classes a direct relationship with the garden and playground.

position.target: younger classes and garden playground relationship
position.rationale: Lower perimeter zone adjacent to the central open space approximates younger-class access.

positive.statement: The circulation areas are pleasant and well dimensioned, with views toward the garden and old town.

position.rationale: Circulation is anchored around the visible central garden and internal perimeter.

positive.statement: The central breathing space supports small-group activities and brings natural light into the building.

position.rationale: Central void is legible in plan and elevations as the building’s breathing space.

positive.statement: The orientation of the classrooms is good.

position.rationale: Classroom zones are approximated along the outer east-south edge with exposed elevations.

positive.statement: The use of wood as covering and structure makes sense in the garden setting and supports rapid dry execution and energy efficiency.

position.rationale: Material is not identifiable; marker follows the visible garden-facing building envelope.

negative.statement: The jury regrets that the existing plane trees were not integrated into the concept.

position.rationale: Existing trees are absent; approximate garden-edge landscape location is marked.

negative.statement: The northern volume could have included more breakthroughs and permeabilities for the neighborhood and future residents.

position.rationale: Northern perimeter volume is visible, while individual openings are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The niche-based changing-room layout is appreciated, but the principle is not applied systematically.

position.rationale: Changing rooms are interior and unidentifiable; east-side middle-level surface provides an approximate anchor.

negative.statement: The desired relationships between certain premises are not always achieved.

position.rationale: Interior adjacency is not represented; central building zone gives a constrained approximation.

negative.statement: The proximity of the northwestern classroom to housing is questionable.

position.rationale: North-west perimeter classroom is approximated where the volume meets adjacent housing frontage.
